articleTitle: Design Space Exploration of Multi-Stage Op Amps by Symbolic Modeling and gm/ID Sampling
publicationTitle: 2023 International Symposium of Electronics Design Automation (ISEDA)
abstract: Design of multi-stage CMOS operational amplifiers (Op Amps) faces unknown design spaces. Designers are often unclear about whether a manually sized circuit has achieved a good tradeoff between multiple design targets and whether other better sizing candidates exit. This paper proposes a design space exploration method for the class of multi-stage Op Amps based on symbolic circuit modeling and gm/ID design variable sampling. This method is easy to implement based on a symbolic circuit modeling tool. Experiment conducted on a three-stage op amp has demonstrated that multiple feasible sizing solutions with explicit performance tradeoffs can be obtained simultaneously.

articleTitle: HybridNet: Dual-Branch Fusion of Geometrical and Topological Views for VLSI Congestion Prediction (Extended Abstract)
publicationTitle: 2023 International Symposium of Electronics Design Automation (ISEDA)
abstract: Accurate early congestion prediction can prevent unpleasant surprises at the routing stage, playing a crucial character in assisting designers to iterate faster in VLSI design cycles. In this paper, we introduce a novel strategy to fully incorporate topological and geometrical features of circuits by making several key designs in our network architecture. To be more specific, we construct two individual graphs (geometry-graph, topology-graph) with distinct edge construction schemes according to their unique properties. We then propose a dual-branch network with different encoder layers in each pathway and aggregate representations with a sophisticated fusion strategy. Our network, named HybridNet, not only provides a simple yet effective way to capture the geometric interactions of cells, but also preserves the original topological relationships in the netlist. Experimental results on the ISPD2015 benchmarks show that we achieve an improvement of 10.9% compared to previous methods.

articleTitle: Power Prediction of RTL-Level Circuits by Using Machine Learning
publicationTitle: 2023 International Symposium of Electronics Design Automation (ISEDA)
abstract: This paper proposes a power prediction framework by using machine learning (ML), which extracts the Hamming distance of the signals from the VCD file generated by RTL simulation as the power features, and uses the power values after placement and routing as the labels. On the 100G network processor (NP) chip adopting 28nm process, the circuit components are divided and the key signals are selected. The power model based on RTL design is constructed, and the power consumption of the system is predicted based on the method of component superposition. The existing experimental results show that the prediction error of component level and system level is less than 15% as a whole, and less than 10% in most cases.

articleTitle: Thermal Evaluation for Monolithic 3D Integrated Circuits Based on Gate-all-Around Transistors
publicationTitle: 2023 International Symposium of Electronics Design Automation (ISEDA)
abstract: In this work, we proposed a monolithic 3D (M3D) integrated circuits (ICs) based on Gate-all-around field effect transistors (GAAFET), and the self-heating effect (SHE) of the M3D ICs is evaluated in detail. A comprehensive thermal evaluation scheme for the M3D ICs is desirable since that higher integration density and more interconnected metals have great obstruction to the thermal dissipation in M3D ICs. Therefore, we systematically investigated the impact of the nano-scale monolithic inter-tier vias (MIVs), power source distribution topology, and the number of GAAFET channels on the thermal characteristic of M3D ICs. In addition, an alternative approach with RC thermal network for accelerating thermal equation solving is presented, which is implemented in a SPICE-based simulator and is capable of fitting finite element method (FEM) simulation results. We expected the comprehensive thermal evaluation for M3D ICs can invoke more research interests in thermal modeling and thermal-aware physical design.

articleTitle: Sizing of Feedforward-Compensated High-Speed Operational Amplifiers
publicationTitle: 2023 International Symposium of Electronics Design Automation (ISEDA)
abstract: This paper studies no-capacitor feedforward (NCFF) compensation multiple-stage operational amplifiers which can achieve very high speed. However, achieving high unity gain frequency (UGF) requires meticulous pole-zero cancellation which is nontrivial to realize in practice. We develop in this paper a deterministic method combining gm/I<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">D</inf>-based sampling and analytical design equation based constraints, a sizing method that is instrumental to realize ad hoc pole-zero allocation. Simulation has confirmed that the sized circuits can achieve substantially high UGF for the NCFF type amplifiers.

articleTitle: A Equivalent Circuit for Rapid Reproduction of IGBT Transient Thermal Impedance Graph
publicationTitle: 2023 International Symposium of Electronics Design Automation (ISEDA)
abstract: The thermal characteristics of insulated gate bipolar transistor (IGBT) module is attracted much attention, since the production consistency and reliability are affected when IGBT works in high temperature environment. Transient thermal impedance is better than steady-state thermal resistance for thermal characterization of the IGBT due to the reason that the IGBT mostly operates in pulsed current mode rather than in DC mode or continuous current mode. In this paper, a simple equivalent circuit is proposed and built in MATLAB Simulink for rapid reproduction of IGBT transient thermal impedance graph given in production datasheets. The reproduced transient thermal impedance graph can help engineers to calculate the current limit of a semiconductor device for different pulse durations.

articleTitle: GPU-Powered Harmonic Balance Analysis in Radio Frequency Circuit Simulation
publicationTitle: 2023 International Symposium of Electronics Design Automation (ISEDA)
abstract: Radio frequency (RF) circuit simulation usually has much larger equation scale than that of the corresponding SPICE model, which poses an immense challenge to meet designer's simulation time requirement with traditional CPU platform. In this paper, we report a GPU-powered harmonic analysis algorithm to address harmonic balance calculation in RF simulation. The major bottlenecks in harmonic balance analysis are presented and solved on GPU platform. Significant performance improvement has been achieved for a large-scale circuit.

articleTitle: Benchmarking Artificial Neural Network Models for Design Technology Co-optimization
publicationTitle: 2023 International Symposium of Electronics Design Automation (ISEDA)
abstract: Device modeling with artificial neural networks (ANN) has been explored in the community. However, figure of merits of ANN models in application scenarios have not been fully validated. In this work, benchmarking of ANN models for design technology co-optimizations of emerging device technologies is performed, in terms of model accuracy, simulation accuracy and speed. First, an approach to address the model discontinuity at the boundary between forward and reverse transistor operation mode in ANN-based compact model (CM) is developed, enhancing the ANN model to pass the Gummel symmetry test (GST). Novel loss functions are then developed for current and charge models with improved accuracy, i.e. within 2% error. Finally, designs and characterizations of GAA standard cell libraries are performed with the ANN model in comparisons to physics-based models. It is found that simulations with the ANN model achieve high accuracy in delay and power consumption predictions within 1% error and speedup by up to 4 times.

articleTitle: An Integrated Logic Function Decomposition Flow for XOR-Majority Graphs
publicationTitle: 2023 International Symposium of Electronics Design Automation (ISEDA)
abstract: Logic function decomposition is critical to logic synthesis. In this paper, we propose an integrated logic function decomposition flow, which consists of disjoint support decomposition, exact synthesis, Shannon decomposition, and the recently proposed majority-of-three (MAJ) decomposition. Through this process, the logic function can be decomposed into any directed acyclic graph (DAG). An experimental evaluation shows that our algorithm leads to better XOR-majority graphs (XMGs) compared to state-of-the-art algorithms. Our experiments show that the proposed method achieves an average of 5% and 6% reduction in the lookup tables (LUTs) size/depth product applied to the EPFL arithmetic and random control benchmarks after LUT mapping, respectively.

articleTitle: HDLcs1.0: A Compiler and Simulator Framework for Hardware Description Language
publicationTitle: 2023 International Symposium of Electronics Design Automation (ISEDA)
abstract: With the increasing scale of integrated circuits, the design of processor chips is highly dependent on EDA tools. Verilog-oriented HDL (Hardware Description Language) processing tools are the key software for front-end design. Apart from commercial EDA tools, open source tools still have room for improvement and optimization. Based on open source software, the required key tools can be further expanded, especially at the gate-level circuit level. This paper presents a compiler and simulator framework HDLcs1.0 for Verilog HDL. Based on LLVM technology and simulator design, we initially established a feasibility framework, which can meet the needs of RTL simulation.

articleTitle: A Review of Intelligent Design for Test Based on Machine Learning
publicationTitle: 2023 International Symposium of Electronics Design Automation (ISEDA)
abstract: In recent years, with the development of post-Moore era, integrated circuit architecture is complex and test cost is increasing. How to apply efficient, reliable, fast and sustainable ideas to integrated circuit design has become a research hotspot in this field. Machine Learning, by virtue of its ability to quickly process abundant data information, shines in the field of Design For Test, which aims to improve the reliability of integrated circuit products and reduce design costs. In this paper, we introduce the application of Machine Learning in scan compression, Automatic Test Pattern Generation algorithm, the Test Pattern Generator in Built-In-Self- Test and test power. In addition, we prospect the foreground application of Machine Learning application in scan test, Automatic Test Pattern Generation, Built-In-Self- Test and test power.

articleTitle: A Novel Method for Automatically Extracting Breakdown Voltage of Zener Diodes from I-V Characteristics Curves
publicationTitle: 2023 International Symposium of Electronics Design Automation (ISEDA)
abstract: Zener diode is widely used in IC design, and its breakdown voltage is an important electrical parameter. However, since the Zener diode has been designed and optimized through the use of a design of experiment (DOE) approach based on TCAD simulations, a large amount of I-V characteristics curves are generated, and then processed by manual method for extracting the breakdown voltages, which is time consuming and error prone. In this paper, a novel numerical method is proposed, mainly including data filling, data smoothing, and anomaly detection. It is successfully applied to automatically extract the breakdown voltages with low human intervention and excellent repeatability.

articleTitle: TED: A Python-Based Analog Design Environment for Agile Circuit Development
publicationTitle: 2023 International Symposium of Electronics Design Automation (ISEDA)
abstract: The paper introduces TED, a Python-based analog hardware design environment that simplifies the design process for both netlist and layout. With its domain-specific syntax and built-in engines for automated placement and routing, TED enables designers to describe analog circuits using fewer lines of code compared to other solutions. Results from experiments show that a SAR-ADC design can be created with just 800 lines of code in TED, while a similar design would require 40,000 lines of code in BAG. Additionally, TED supports technology-generic design, allowing for highly reusable designs across different process technologies and enabling a no-human-in-the-loop design process when transitioning from one technology to another, saving significant time and effort in repeated design work.

articleTitle: Stochastic EUV Resist Model
publicationTitle: 2023 International Symposium of Electronics Design Automation (ISEDA)
abstract: The stochastic effects in photoresist patterning is of great concern in the implementation of EUV lithography. The stochastic nature of EUV chemically amplified resist requires new modeling approaches rather than the continuous model used in DUV. In this paper, a stochastic model based on Gillespie algorithm is introduced, which subdivides the resist volume into many rectangular small cells and simulates the reaction-diffusion behavior of molecules in a cell volume according to carefully calculated probability. In addition, we further explore the influence of the cell size on the stochastic model. There is an optimal cell size in consideration of precision and running time. When cell size is sufficiently large, the results will approximate to the continuous model.

articleTitle: A Variation-Aware Lagrangian Relaxation-Based Gate Sizing Framework for Timing Optimization
publicationTitle: 2023 International Symposium of Electronics Design Automation (ISEDA)
abstract: State-of-the-art work in academia on discrete gate sizing using Lagrangian relaxation (LR) has implemented the best leakage power reduction for runtime acceleration. In this paper, a new objective function is constructed by considering the gate-level delay variation to adapt to the optimization requirements of near-threshold circuits. We optimize the power consumption of the circuit while avoiding the deterioration of the worst delay of the critical path of the circuit. Based on the TSMC 28nm HPC Plus CMOS process at near-threshold voltage, the ISCAS89 test circuit is used for verification and comparative analysis. The validation results show that the proposed gate sizing optimization method can reduce the 3φ delay of critical paths by at least 5.63% on average compared to the state-of-the-art cell sizing method without introducing additional circuit power consumption.

articleTitle: Variation-Aware Clock Path Timing Model in Near-Threshold Voltage
publicationTitle: 2023 International Symposium of Electronics Design Automation (ISEDA)
abstract: A clock path timing modeling method for near- threshold voltage circuits is adopted in this paper, which is composed of clock cell models and interconnect models using regression fitting methods. The proposed near-threshold clock tree timing modeling methods are validated on the ISCAS89 benchmark circuits and the Cortex-M3 benchmark circuit with the SMIC40LL process. The results show that compared with the clock tree obtained by the EDA tool (IC Compiler), the method proposed in this thesis reduces the clock skew by 35.1% on average and the clock skew variation (standard deviation of clock skew) by 37.3% on average.

articleTitle: Average-Approximation SIP Algorithms Used to Improve Accuracy of RC Model Order Reduction
publicationTitle: 2023 International Symposium of Electronics Design Automation (ISEDA)
abstract: This paper presents the Average-Approximation Sparse Implicit Projection (AASIP) algorithm, which enhances the accuracy of the lossless correction factor in Sparse Implicit Projection (SIP) by employing the mean fitting correction. AASIP improves the approximate accuracy of RC-netlist reduction compared to conventional SIP, while also addressing the challenges of high-order moment matching in SIP. The correctness and feasibility of the proposed algorithm are demonstrated through netlist examples.

articleTitle: An Automated Propagation Approach that Promotes and Demotes the Timing Exception Between Hierarchical Blocks and Flat Design
publicationTitle: 2023 International Symposium of Electronics Design Automation (ISEDA)
abstract: An automated propagation approach is presented to achieve the timing constraint promotion and demotion between hierarchical blocks and flat design. The propagation scheme deals with several types of timing constraints, such as timing exceptions, clock definitions and boundary conditions. To simplify the classification, the propagation scheme divides the timing constraints into a few groups so that the promotion and demotion methodology of each group can propagate kinds of timing constraint types, which have similar options and grammar. In other words, each group reuses one promotion and demotion algorithm to propagate several timing constraints between hierarchical blocks and flat design. In particular, this paper focuses on the timing exception's promotion and demotion algorithm, which combines a new Breadth First Search(BFS) with a new Depth First Search(DFS) to adapt the graph structure of real circuit and realize high accuracy and high efficiency as well. The DFS method is improved in aspect of timing path traversing. Based on the character of timing path, a new strategy is applied to avoid to traverse the fake path, in which there isn't a connection between part of nodes at current depth level but there is connection among the nodes at next depth level. On the other hand, the proposed new BFS approach uses a parallel process to achieve high speed. To verify the performance of the proposed propagation scheme, an experimental environment is built. The test environment is utilized to evaluate the circuit design in terms of accuracy and efficiency. In addition, the circuit is a signoff design and the timing constraints contain different timing paths and structural complexities. The experimental result shows that the proposed approach can accurately propagate the timing constraints between hierarchical blocks and flat design. It also performs robustness character according to various timing exceptions. Moreover, the combined BFS & DFS algorithm reduces by about 40% runtime compared to DFS method.

articleTitle: A Synthesis Method for Verilog Case Statement Using Mux-and-Inverter Graph
publicationTitle: 2023 International Symposium of Electronics Design Automation (ISEDA)
abstract: Crossbar architectures are widely used in high-performance network switches, such as connecting PEs in multiprocessor systems. The crossbar is usually synthesized by CASE statements in Verilog, and its delay largely affects the performance of the whole design. We proposed a multi-strategy synthesis method exclusively for CASE statements. Based on mux-and-inverter graph (MAIG), this method simplifies selection logic using the Boolean characteristic. Experimental result shows that this method could bring 4.30% less area and 16.3% less delay than Yosys.

articleTitle: A Data-Driven CMP Layout-Dependent Effect Modeling Methodology
publicationTitle: 2023 International Symposium of Electronics Design Automation (ISEDA)
abstract: We propose a data-driven modeling methodology to predict layout-dependent effects (LDE) in chemical mechanical polishing (CMP). The proposed model accurately predicts the surface micro-topography after polishing for any given layout design. Our method relies solely on silicon data, and no prior knowledge of underlying mechanisms is required to build up the models. Experimental results at different process nodes demonstrate the advantages of our method in terms of accuracy, speed, and applicability.

articleTitle: An Effective Parallel Acceleration Method for Transient Simulation of Large-Scale Power Ground Network
publicationTitle: 2023 International Symposium of Electronics Design Automation (ISEDA)
abstract: With the improvement of integrated circuit technique, chips have developed from large-scale to very large-scale integration (VLSI). The design of power/ground (P/G) network becomes a key factor limiting chip's rapid development, especially in the design of VLSI. Some classical algorithms, such as random walk, become difficult to perform transient simulation as the scale of P/G increases. In this paper, fast sparse matrix addition and distributed parallel acceleration method is proposed to accelerate transient analysis of P/G network without considering the specific topology of the network. Compared to the single-process solver, transient analysis of a P/G network example with around 5 million nodes can be accelerated 2.69X times by the proposed method, while keeping a high-precision solution.

articleTitle: Iterative and Verifiable Retiming for FPGA Performance Optimization
publicationTitle: 2023 International Symposium of Electronics Design Automation (ISEDA)
abstract: Reducing the critical path delay is the key to optimizing the circuit performance since it determines the maximum operating frequency. Retiming is a synchronous circuit transformation that can reduce the critical path delay by moving registers across combinational circuit elements. Compared with ASIC, more than 55% physical delays of FPGA come from the interconnection. Hence it is beneficial to use these interconnection delays for FPGA retiming. However, FPGA retiming is normally carried out before or during placement and routing without precise static timing analysis (STA), which leads to inaccurate physical timing optimization results. In addition, it is also a difficult task to verify the functional equivalence of circuits before and after retiming. In this paper, we propose an iterative and verifiable retiming algorithm, which extracts critical path information from the STA report and iteratively performs retiming by modifying BLIF netlist based on the physical interconnection delay, rather than the logic depth. Our experimental results based on VPR benchmark demonstrate that our method can reduce critical path delay by 5% on average while ensuring the functional equivalence. Compared to retiming in ABC, which lacks physical timing information, our method achieves smaller delay with fewer registers used. Compared to Vivado retiming gain on Virtex-7, the proposed method can achieve an 1.3% retiming gain improvement on k6_Frac_N10_Frac_Chain_Mem32K_40nm in VPR.

articleTitle: An Accurate Statistical Cell Delay Model Considering Multiple-Input Switching Effect
publicationTitle: 2023 International Symposium of Electronics Design Automation (ISEDA)
abstract: To restrict the storage overhead, traditional statistical static timing analysis (SSTA) employs a delay model that assumes only a single input switches for a cell during a transition, while all other side inputs are held constant. Nevertheless, ignoring the impact of multiple-input switching (MIS) can lead to an overestimation or an underestimation of a cell delay, causing over-designing for the timing margin. In this paper, we present a novel approach using expected scale factors to assess the impact of MIS on statistical timing analysis. Meanwhile, an accurate cell delay calibration method considering skewness and kurtosis is proposed to measure the +/-30σ cell delay. Tested by cells with TSMC 28nm technology, our model can estimate the +/-3σ point with similar accuracy comparing to state-of-the-art technology in single-input switching (SIS) mode. Moreover, in near-/sub-threshold voltage, the cell delay computed by our model in MIS mode differs from the SPICE-computed delay by less than 4%, which infers significant improvement over MIS delay models proposed by prior studies.

articleTitle: Optimization of Multiplexer Combination in RTL Logic Synthesis
publicationTitle: 2023 International Symposium of Electronics Design Automation (ISEDA)
abstract: The paper presents an optimizable multiplexer combination in logic synthesis of RTL level circuits. There are often some redundant multiplexers in the circuit, the deletion or optimization of these multiplexers does not affect the design behavior of circuits. Therefore, we propose a special multiplexer combination. It can be optimized on the premise that the logic function of the circuit remains unchanged, and it can also be merged with other traditional optimizable multiplexers to further optimize the circuit. In the paper, we use examples to optimize and verify, the results show that the optimizable combination can effectively reduce the number of multiplexers, The results show that the optimizable combination can significantly reduce the number of multiplexer elements, and appears more frequently and probably in the circuit. The optimizable combination is feasible and practical in the logic synthesis of circuits, which can effectively reduce the number of elements and design scale of the circuit.

articleTitle: A Physical Insight Based Neural Network Model for Small Signal Behavior of MOSFET in Terahertz Applications
publicationTitle: 2023 International Symposium of Electronics Design Automation (ISEDA)
abstract: In this paper, a physical insight based neural network small signal MOSFET model is proposed, which can accurately and efficiently describe the high-frequency behavior of MOSFET. By incorporating prior physical knowledge in the preprocessing stage of neural networks, the model demonstrates the enhancement of precision and reliability and is capable of describing non-quasi-static effects as well as other parasitic effects and second-order effects precisely. The proposed model is validated with the small signal data obtained by TCAD simulation up to 1THz, and the model can predict high-frequency y-parameters with 3σ error less than 3%.

articleTitle: A Learning-Based Method for Gate Delay Prediction under NBTI and Process Variation Effects
publicationTitle: 2023 International Symposium of Electronics Design Automation (ISEDA)
abstract: As the transistor process technology shrinks to nanoscale, aging and process variation effects become dominant issues affecting the chip reliability. Analytical evaluation at the early stages of chip design is critical to ensure that the chip will function correctly throughout its entire life cycle. In this paper, a machine learning model named Gaussian Process Regression (GPR) is proposed for predicting gate delay, which considers aging and process variation effects jointly. The experiment uses commercial 28 nm technology to simulate typical types of logic gates and verify the performance of GPR. Our approach can obtain accurate prediction with rRMSE score of 0.19% and MAE score of 0.14%, and significant runtime speed-up with 1000X speedup, with minimal loss of accuracy compared to the golden data.

articleTitle: Structure-Preserving Model Order Reduction for Thermal Analysis
publicationTitle: 2023 International Symposium of Electronics Design Automation (ISEDA)
abstract: Accurate and fast thermal analysis is important for the 3D IC and SiP design with increasing complexity. Compact Thermal Model(CTM) combined with Model Order Reduction(MOR) is widely used in fast thermal analysis. However, the heterogeneous distribution structure is destroyed in traditional MOR strategies. In this paper, we propose a heuristic strategy to cut the original network into several blocks, which is followed by adaptive block-based MOR. Experiments show that compared with the state-of-the-art method, our method preserves the block structure in much less MOR time without burden on accuracy and subsequent simulation.

articleTitle: Wafer map defect pattern classification based on multi-scale depthwise separable convolution
publicationTitle: 2023 International Symposium of Electronics Design Automation (ISEDA)
abstract: Wafer map defect recognition can help engineers quickly locate problems in the IC manufacturing process, which is critical for improving the yield and reliability of IC manufacturing process. In previous studies, some machine learning methods were proposed to replace manual identification. However, targeted optimization for the characteristics of wafer defect pattern data has not been considered in previous studies. In this paper, we proposed a classifier based on a multi-scale depthwise separable convolutional (MDSC) neural network that captures the spatial correlation within each channel through multi-scale convolution. This combination can better express the global and local features of the wafer, thereby improving the accuracy of model recognition. We adopted the methods of label smoothing and quality focal loss (QFL) to address the issue of data imbalance, which further improved the accuracy of recognition and finally reached 98% accuracy on the test set.

articleTitle: A SAT Enhanced Word-Level Solver for Constrained Random Simulation
publicationTitle: 2023 International Symposium of Electronics Design Automation (ISEDA)
abstract: As the complexity of the hardware design grows, verification has been widely acknowledged as the bottleneck during the overall design flow. In simulation-based verification, the random stimuli that satisfy specified mixed Boolean/bit-vector constraints are generated to validate the design behaviors. The efficiency of the design flow is heavily dependent on the performance of the constraint solver that produces the legal stimuli. In this paper, we first discuss the challenge of solving constraints with some specific operators such as IF-THEN-ELSE (ITE), IMPLIES, and Boolean OR using a word-level solver. To address this, a Boolean Satisfiability (SAT) solver is introduced to prune constraints and compress the search space for the word-level solver. Experimental results demonstrate the proposed hybrid solver outperforms the original word-level solver by about 50% on average in test cases with these specific operators.

articleTitle: Design and Optimization of Interface Circuits of MEMS Thermal Wind Speed Sensor Based on a Macro Model
publicationTitle: 2023 International Symposium of Electronics Design Automation (ISEDA)
abstract: In this paper, interface circuits of MEMS thermal wind sensor that compensating system temperature drift are designed based on a macro model. The macro model realizes the co-simulation of the sensor and circuits by coupling thermal field, flow field and electric field with the combination of linear time irrelevant (LTI) reduced-order model (ROM) method, convective heat transfer formula and Verilog-A, temperature effects on the sensor are also taken into account. Based on the model, a constant temperature difference (CTD) control circuit is designed and optimized, which consists of a two-Wheatstone bridges structure and two amplifiers in general. It compensates the temperature drift caused by the mismatch of the temperature coefficient of the heating resistor and the ambient temperature measurement resistor in CTD control. To solve the temperature drift problem of the sensor output voltage, a compensation circuit based on a reference voltage generation circuit with adjustable temperature coefficient is designed to meet the needs of integration and low power consumption instead of using micro control unit (MCU) for software compensation. The error of measured wind speed is less than 0.8m/s. The results shows that the proposed circuits meet the requirements of the sensor system, and the design flow with the aid of the macro model has high efficiency and convenience.

articleTitle: Exploration of FPGA PLB Architecture Base on LUT and Microgates
publicationTitle: 2023 International Symposium of Electronics Design Automation (ISEDA)
abstract: Because of the logic redundancy of look-up table (LUT) based field programmable gate array (FPGA), we explore a series of programmable logic block (PLB) architectures to increase logic density by adding different kinds of microgates including AND gate and exclusive-OR gate. Because individual LUT inputs have different delays to the output, adding microgates to the shortest input-output path does not influence the LUT critical path delay. To evaluate the proposed PLB architectures, the Boolean matching based on disjoint-support decomposition (DSD) library in ABC is used to realize technology mapping and followed by VPR 8.0 to pack, place and route. Evaluation results based on VTR and Koios benchmarks show that the proposed PLB architecture by adding two AND gates to LUT6 can achieve the best performance, which reduces the logic depth, the utilization of PLBs, and the critical path delay by 19.8%, 4.36%, and 6.25% respectively on average compared to Intel Stratix-10 PLB architecture in VTR.

articleTitle: A Multi-Dimensional Weight Partition Algorithm for FPGA Prototype Simulation
publicationTitle: 2023 International Symposium of Electronics Design Automation (ISEDA)
abstract: As the complexity of circuit design increases, single FPGA can no longer meet the requirements of logic simulation and rapid prototyping, so the circuit design needs to be partitioned into multiple parts, and then it can use multiple FPGA systems for simulation. When RTL-level code is modeled as an undirected graph, the weight of vertex is multidimensional and the edge is weighted. In order to meet the demand of multi-FPGA platform, we modeled the RTL-level code into an undirected graph, whose vertex weight is multidimensional, corresponding to different resources of FPGA platform, and the edge is weighted.A new partitioning algorithm should satisfy the following two requirements. Firstly, the multi-dimensional weight of each partition is below the FPGA threshold in each dimension. Secondly, the partition algorithm should minimize max_cut, where max_cut is the largest cut size between all partitions. In this paper, we propose a partition algorithm that meets the above requirements.

articleTitle: Real-Time Optimization Design of GAAFETs Based on Machine Learning Method
publicationTitle: 2023 International Symposium of Electronics Design Automation (ISEDA)
abstract: This paper proposes a real-time optimization design of GAAFET based on machine learning method, using artificial neural network (ANN) to train the deep learning model, whose input and output are process structure parameters and electrical characteristic parameters, respectively. Our framework can automatically update the deep learning model with the error between the prediction and the actual, so as to realize the automatic training and decision-making. Our optimized design method has been partially confirmed on the 5nm stacked gate all around (GAA) nanosheet transistor (NST) platform, 1) the prediction time is 33962 times faster than traditional TCAD, 2) compared with the TCAD simulation results, the model achieves 99.7 % accuracy, therefore, the process time for device development is also massively shortened. At the same time, this framework is applied to the process of finding the optimal solution in the future.

articleTitle: A Fast Escape Router for Large-Scale Staggered-Pin-Array PCBs
publicationTitle: 2023 International Symposium of Electronics Design Automation (ISEDA)
abstract: Compared with regular pin array, staggered pin array enjoys a larger pin density in printed circuit boards (PCBs). However, the routing efficiency and scalability are degraded due to the increased routing complexity in staggered pin array PCBs. This paper proposes a fast escape routing method for staggered pin arrays, which extends an ultrafast rule-based escape routing algorithm from Manhattan routing to diagonal routing. Experimental results show that, compared with the state-of-the-art escape routing method, our proposed method enjoys notable improvements in both effectiveness and efficiency in routing large-scale staggered-pin-array PCBs. 100x speedup in runtime is obtained by our method. Our method also demonstrates the potential for efficiently routing routing large-scale designs with up to 160k terminals.

articleTitle: An Effective Macro Placement Algorithm Based On Curiosity-Driven Reinforcement Learning
publicationTitle: 2023 International Symposium of Electronics Design Automation (ISEDA)
abstract: In mixed-size circuit designs, due to the numerous connections with standard cells and huge sizes of macros, the positions of macros greatly affect the placement of standard cells and then the layout quality. In this work, we use an on-policy reinforcement learning method to train an agent from scratch and make the agent learn macro placement. To satisfy the non-overlap constraint of macro placement, we design a fast non-overlapping algorithm. To get better feature extraction of global and local state information, we adopt a convolutional neural network (CNN) and an edge-based graph neural network (Edge-GNN). In addition, we add intrinsic reward as the curiosity in the reward design to encourage the agent to explore, helping the agent better understand how to place macros effectively. Experiment results show that our proposed framework is more effective in optimizing the wirelength of the placement compared with a simulated annealing method.

articleTitle: Multiple-Input Switching Modeling with Graph Neural Network
publicationTitle: 2023 International Symposium of Electronics Design Automation (ISEDA)
abstract: Multiple Input Switching (MIS) poses great challenge in Static Timing Analysis (STA) with unexpected setup or hold violations due to temporal proximity among transitions at different inputs of gate. Most prior empirical and learning based models are ad hoc techniques which should be applied to each gate separately and ignore the relation of MIS with transistor-level gate topology, leading to poor estimation accuracy and/or considerable characterization effort. In this work, a Graph Neural Network (GNN) based model is proposed to predict MIS-SIS Difference (MSD), which is trained jointly as a unified model by mapping transistor-level gate topology into nodes and edges of graph. The proposed model was validated under TSMC 16nm process for a set of multiple-input gates and paths from ISCAS‘85 and TAU benchmarks. Experimental results demonstrate excellent agreement with golden SPICE simulation results by this work with NRMSE error less than 0.73% in average for all validated gates. Comparing with prior learning based approach, our model achieves 2.7× characterization effort reduction with comparative accuracy. The predicted path delays with MIS effect with our model is highly consistent to SPICE simulation results with the average error 2.0%.

articleTitle: Flexible Acceleration Framework for Dense/Sparse Matrix Multiplication on Versal ACAP
publicationTitle: 2023 International Symposium of Electronics Design Automation (ISEDA)
abstract: Matrix multiplication (MM) is one of the most commonly applied operations in various application domains, including deep learning, recommendation system, robotics, etc. AMD Xilinx Versal ACAP combines optimized ASIC engines (AIE) and programmable logic (FPGA) with hardened DSPs and becomes the ideal platform for diverse MM-intensive applications due to strong computing power and sufficient reconfigurability. However, the architecture heterogeneity also brings outstanding programming challenges and constitutes barriers for non-expert users to accelerate their target applications. The situation even worsens when the acceleration system is composed of various accelerators, such as dense or sparse MM accelerators under different configurations. In this paper, we propose FlexVA, a flexible acceleration framework, which supports general operations, including both dense and sparse matrix multiplication, and targets Versal ACAP architecture. FlexVA provides convenient description tools to program accelerator candidates under flexible configurations as accelerator templates with parameters. The framework not only allows users to select, configure, and compose accelerators flexibly but also provides an XRT-based software runtime with scheduling strategies that are also configurable by users. We implement and optimize both the dense-dense (GEMM) and sparse-dense (SpMM) accelerators with FlexVA.

articleTitle: An Aging Small-signal Modeling Method of Microwave Transistors Using GA-ELM Neural Network
publicationTitle: 2023 International Symposium of Electronics Design Automation (ISEDA)
abstract: In this paper, an aging small-signal S-parameters modeling method for microwave transistors is explored using a genetic algorithm (GA) to optimize the Extreme Learning Machine (ELM) neural network. A dual GA-ELM neural network architecture was used to simulate the fresh S-parameters of InP heterojunction bipolar transistor (HBT) devices and the degradation of S-parameters after accelerated aging, respectively. Good agreement was achieved between measured and predicted results of the fresh and aging S-parameters within a frequency range of 0.1 to 40 GHz.

articleTitle: Fast and Accurate Electromigration Analysis of Multi-Segment Wires
publicationTitle: 2023 International Symposium of Electronics Design Automation (ISEDA)
abstract: Electromigration (EM) in interconnects has many reliability issues in current VLSI technologies. In chips, interconnects usually consist of multi-segment wires, and the electromagnetic effects of each segment are not independent and must be considered simultaneously. However, most of the existing EM modeling methods focus on single-segment wires. Numerous calls to the basic EM model to simulate EM stresses are time-consuming in the sign off phase. Therefore, we propose an accurate and fast EM stress model based on optimized back propagation neural networks i.e.GA-BP, which can predict the transient EM stress of three typical wires at different sizes and different current densities. Compared with conventional BPNN, the GA-BP show significant improvement in convergence speed and ability. According to the experimental results, our work obtain an EM stress prediction accuracy larger than 0.997 compared with golden results generated via the commercial software COMSOL. In addition, it can provide EM stress results in an average of 0.023s. Our model has application value in the future to speed up the EM stress prediction of large-scale interconnects.

articleTitle: A Statistical Evaluation Method to Quantify the Runtime Uncertainty of Accelerator-rich SoC Targeting EDA Acceleration
publicationTitle: 2023 International Symposium of Electronics Design Automation (ISEDA)
abstract: Integrating a host CPU with domain-specific accelerators is a promising way to improve the performance/power/area of EDA acceleration in the post-Moore age. But it is hard to estimate the runtime performance of the accelerator-rich SoC in the early stage, especially considering the uncertainty produced by PVT variation. To predict and further avoid the architectural risk, we propose a statistical model to evaluate the runtime distribution while targeting EDA acceleration. We first collect the dataset by the Latin hypercube sampling method and dump the output runtime data via gem5-SALAM simulator. After transforming the original dataset into the Gauss distribution through box-cox transformation, we integrate the least square boosting regression to achieve the deterministic estimation. Then we inject the uncertainties of frequency and unit yield, and thus the predictions become distributions. Based on the statistical evaluation method with a 4.3% normalized MSE, we can find that the experimental performance is usually worse than the original deterministic estimation, which proves the architectural risk.

articleTitle: A Multi-Objective Optimization Algorithm Based on Deep Learning for Circuit Partition
publicationTitle: 2023 International Symposium of Electronics Design Automation (ISEDA)
abstract: Circuit partition is a critical step during Three-dimensional integrated circuit(3D IC) physical design. The quality of circuit partition directly affects the subsequent processes(placement, clock-tree synchronization, route, etc.). Circuit partition is the process that divides a circuit composed of logic gates into subsets with the objective of minimizing the inter connection of subsets and balancing the sum of modules weights between subsets. It can be modeled as a graph partition problem, which is known to be NP-hard. Compared with the traditional graph partition problem, in order to make full use of the space resources of 3D chips, circuit partition pays more attention to the balance between subsets. In this paper, we propose a deep learning-based multi-objective optimization algorithm. Our algorithm uses multiple branch feature extractors(based on GraphSAGE) to learn the features and topological relationships of nodes, and then generates node embedding. Finally, our algorithm obtains the circuit partitioning strategy by using node allocator(based on FC). Compared to the state-of-the-art graph partition(metis), our algorithm improves the balance of partition(2×), and slightly reduces cut-edge quality.

articleTitle: Back-Scaling Based Exponential Integrator Method with Multi-Process Parallel Processing for Transient Power/Ground Network Analysis
publicationTitle: 2023 International Symposium of Electronics Design Automation (ISEDA)
abstract: The exponential integrator (EI) method has proven to be an effective technique for accelerating transient circuit simulation. Owing to its higher accuracy order, EI can use larger step sizes to speed up the simulation without compromising accuracy. However, leaping with large steps may sometimes omit some fine-grained variations of the waveforms, especially for power/ground network analysis where over/under-shoots are important. We propose a back-scaling technique to address this issue to complete the detailed waveform between two consecutive time points in EI simulation without extra LU factorizations or triangular solves. The key is to re-use the Krylov subspace generated at the starting time point and scale the step size to obtain solutions at any place between the two endpoints, exploiting the special scaling invariant property of the Krylov subspace in EI. In addition, we also develop a multi-process parallelization based on MPI to accelerate the back-scaling process. Numerical experiments are conducted to demonstrate the accuracy and efficacy of the proposed method.

articleTitle: DAC-CPPR: A fast and accurate approach for common path pessimism removal with divide and conquer on the clock tree
publicationTitle: 2023 International Symposium of Electronics Design Automation (ISEDA)
abstract: To reduce the redundant pessimism in static timing analysis, common path pessimism removal (CPPR) is widely used as a pivotal step. However, as the amount of pessimism that needs to be removed is path-specific, solving the CPPR problem is very expensive and has become the hurdle in deploying the technology. Even though there exit efficient design-specific pruning heuristics, their performance cannot be guaranteed. In this paper, we introduce DAC-CPPR, a CPPR algorithm that is both efficient and with provably good performance. It is based on Divide and Conquer technique on the clock tree. We prove the algorithm has a logarithmic time complexity proportional to the clock tree nodes. Experimental results demonstrate the effectiveness and efficiency of our algorithms.

articleTitle: Incremental Verilog Parser
publicationTitle: 2023 International Symposium of Electronics Design Automation (ISEDA)
abstract: Traditional hardware language parsers typically employ full-file compilation, which requires the entire file to be re-parsed even for minor modifications to the design code. This can result in long re-compilation times, particularly for industrial-grade chip designs that may have millions or even tens of millions of lines of code. This paper introduces an incremental syntax analysis technique for hardware languages and presents an incremental Verilog parser, Stagira 1.1, that utilizes this technique. Stagira 1.1 performs syntax analysis at the module level, determines the dependency relationships between modules based on module instantiation statements, and stores the abstract syntax tree structure and dependency table in binary files. The dependency table allows the user to recompile only the specified module and its related modules upon code changes, significantly reducing re-compilation times and enhancing the efficiency of chip development. The development of incremental parsers like Stagira 1.1 provides a solid foundation for the creation of various incremental EDA tools, which are essential for efficient hardware language parsing.

articleTitle: Two Data Driven CMP Modeling Methods for DFM
publicationTitle: 2023 International Symposium of Electronics Design Automation (ISEDA)
abstract: Chemical Mechanical Polishing(CMP) plays an essential role in the fabrication of advanced integrated circuits, and the flatness of the wafer surface after CMP directly affects the stability of subsequent processes and chip yields. Mechanism- based modeling is difficult. Data-driven approaches offer a different approach to CMP modeling. In this paper, we use artificial neural networks and Group Method of Data Handling(GMDH) polynomial networks to build CMP models based on real silicon data, and compare and analyze the two approaches.

articleTitle: Parametric design of asynchronous SAR ADC with redundancy
publicationTitle: 2023 International Symposium of Electronics Design Automation (ISEDA)
abstract: The successive approximation register (SAR) ADC is particularly suitable for modern technology and low power consumption due to its simple analog structure. By adding redundancy, SARADC can gain digital error correction capability to rectify the mismatch of capacitance arrays. SARADC chips typically possess specific precision and technology. SARADC can be coded to adjust the precision and technology, and generate the layout automatically, based on TED Electronic Design (TED). This paper presents a parametric SARADC generator capable of producing asynchronous SARADCs with redundancy in different processes, ranging from 5 to 10 bits.

articleTitle: 3D Compact Thermal Model and its Application on Fast Chip Level Thermal Simulation
publicationTitle: 2023 International Symposium of Electronics Design Automation (ISEDA)
abstract: This paper presents a three dimensional fast thermal simulation tool named 3DDCTM for chip level integrated circuits, which is developed based on Compact Thermal Model (CTM) and Model Order Reduction (MOR) algorithm. The tool provides various types of solution including steady conduction, unsteady conduction, and a Smart Compact Thermal Model for Dynamic Thermal Management (DTM). A nonuniform orthogonal grid generation module is integrated into the tool and could automate generate body fit grids based on presetting grid constraints. 3DDCTM requires much less computational time with a similar accuracy compared to traditional thermal simulators. Due to the ability of reading JEDEC the exchange of electronic thermal system level simulation models (ECXML), the present tool supports import model established by commercial simulators, which greatly enhances the extent of the tool. The results could be loaded and shown in the open source visualization application Paraview. The thermal behavior of a chip with high-end packages is investigated for verification. The simulation results are discussed and it is found that the present thermal tool shows an excellent performance not only on good accuracy but also less computational time compared with typical thermal commercial software.

articleTitle: A GPU-Accelerated ADI Method for Thermal Simulation of Liquid-Cooled 3-D ICs
publicationTitle: 2023 International Symposium of Electronics Design Automation (ISEDA)
abstract: This paper presents an efficient methodology for the transient thermal simulation of liquid-cooled 3-D integrated circuits (ICs). A compact thermal network model and the alternating direction implicit (ADI) method accelerated by graphics processing unit (GPU) are employed to improve computational efficiency. The simulation result shows that the proposed method can significantly reduce the computational time cost while maintaining satisfactory accuracy.

articleTitle: Geometry Dependent Multi-stage Compact Thermal Model for Advanced Nanosheet FETs
publicationTitle: 2023 International Symposium of Electronics Design Automation (ISEDA)
abstract: Gate-All-Around Nanosheet FETs (NSFETs) are promising candidates for sub 5nm node, however, the aggressive scaling NSFETs are susceptible to the self-heating effect (SHE). A precise thermal model compatible with industry SPICE model, e.g. BSIMCMG, is critical to improve the yield of NSFET-based integrated circuit design and to reduce the development timeline of the advanced process. In this paper, we propose a geometry dependent multi-stage thermal RC network to accurately predict self-heating over a wide frequency range, from DC to THz, for the advanced NSFETs, which is validated by the transient thermal simulations based on 3-D Finite Element Modeling (FEM) method. The proposed compact thermal model enables to take the impacts of nanosheet width, number of stacks (gate fingers) and gate length into account, where the stage and model parameters of the thermal RC model are determined by Bayesian deconvolution and Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO) methods, respectively. The underlying physical understandings behind the geometry dependent thermal behaviors are discussed in detail.

articleTitle: System Static Timing Analysis Method Based on Hierarchization
publicationTitle: 2023 International Symposium of Electronics Design Automation (ISEDA)
abstract: Static timing analysis (STA) is a technology used to verify the timing of digital design. In the simulation and verification of VLSI, multiple FPGA chips work together. To obtain the timing performance of the system, it is necessary to establish a timing analysis model from the perspective of multiple FPGA systems. And STA will be called many times to verify the circuit timing in the logic synthesis, placement and routing stages of the design, which makes the development of fast system level STA algorithm a key. In this paper, a multi-core accelerated system STA algorithm is implemented. Based on the logical hierarchy on the timing path, the delay on the path is solved in parallel by using the non-correlation of the data at the same hierarchy, and achieves 3.9 times of parallel speed-up on 8 cores of the CPU.

articleTitle: Test Vector Generation for Array-form Multipliers Using a Genetic Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2023 International Symposium of Electronics Design Automation (ISEDA)
abstract: Digital multipliers are often designed in the array form. Traditional timing closure of multipliers is issued by static timing analysis (STA) which only gives a conservative timing report. Sometimes we would like to find the critical paths of a multiplier array and the corresponding input words (test vectors) that activate such critical paths. This is a very time-consuming task if using an exhaustive test vector enumeration method. There exists only one heuristic method in the open literature that can generate suboptimal test patterns corresponding to relatively long critical paths for multipliers with quite long word lengths. However, this method does not guarantee that the generated test vectors would activate the longest critical paths. In this paper we propose a genetic algorithm (GA) to conduct the search of the longest critical path test patterns for the array multipliers using carry-save adders (CSA). Experiments show that the GA method can find the longest critical paths for a set of CSA array multipliers up to the word length of 21 bits. Improvements over the previous method have been observed.

articleTitle: Transistor Compact Model Based On Gradient Constrainted Convolution Neural Network
publicationTitle: 2023 International Symposium of Electronics Design Automation (ISEDA)
abstract: In semiconductor research, the characteristic curves of analog devices under different combinations of process and device structure parameters are very important. Traditional TCAD simulation plays a very important role, but building a compact model based on quantum physics requires a lot of effort and time, and shows relatively weak technical adaptability. The derivative of the model output may also lose continuity. In order to solve these problems, this work proposes a gradient supervised convolution neural network model with adaptive dynamic adjustment of learning rate. It is employed to model the I-V characteristics of GAA and PLANAR devices and achieves the continuity of higher-order derivatives. In addition, this work designs effective data preprocessing and new weighted loss function to enhance model expressivity. The I-V curves and physical verification of GAA and PLANAR devices by the proposed model show that the model can obtain high-precision fitting and achieve high-order differentiable continuity.

articleTitle: Generation of Series-Parallel Multilevel Transistor Networks Based on BDDs
publicationTitle: 2023 International Symposium of Electronics Design Automation (ISEDA)
abstract: Most of the current VLSI physical design flow is based on the standard cell model. The optimization of circuit is limited by the logic functions contained in the standard cell library. The customization of corresponding standard cells of typical logic in a design can bring better implementation. The topology implementation with minimum transistor count for a specific logic function can provide effective evaluation for the feasibility and benefit of logic function customization, and assist in standard cell design. In this work, a method based on BDD is proposed to automatically generate transistor networks with minimum transistor count using redundant logic expressions as inputs. This work aims to make the generated transistor network meet the reliability requirements of advanced technology. For example, the generated transistor network contains two logical complementary planes and is a serial-parallel network (excluding bridge structure), with the constraints on maximum number of serial/parallel transistors for each plane. When the input logic function is too large to be implemented by a single level transistor network, the proposed method automatically generates a multilevel transistor network with a minimum transistor count.

articleTitle: A Highly Collaborative EDA Toolset for Design Technology Co-Optimization Towards Analog and Mixed Signal Circuits
publicationTitle: 2023 International Symposium of Electronics Design Automation (ISEDA)
abstract: In order to meet the high performance and reliability requirements of industrial chips, especially analog and mixed-signal (AMS) circuits, the process technology and circuits design need to be highly collaborative. In this paper, a design technology co-optimization (DTCO) simulation toolset is developed. It includes two parts: process technology tool and circuit design tool. The first part, process technology tool, includes high precision TCAD device simulation and testkey layout autogeneration tool. For TCAD simulation, especially LDMOS that based on drift-diffusion models, a particular hexahedral mesh was used to lower mesh complexity and improve numerical accuracy. This tool can accurately calculate key electrical parameters such as R<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">dson</inf>, BV<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">off</inf>, V<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">th</inf>, BV<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">on</inf>, etc. The automatic layout generator tool was used to generate the testkey layout for WAT testing, device modeling and reliability testing etc. The second part, circuit design tool, consists of unified automatic signal sampling scheme for XPS/Cosim verification, making finally packaged real number; Different quick waveform storage method to accelerate results check; and whole chip over-voltage (OV)/forward diodes check for customized process. This DTCO simulation toolset is verified by a power management chip PMIC620 which includes analog and mixed signal circuits, based on the 0.18um 40V BCD technology. The chip is tapeout with first silicon successful.

articleTitle: Research on Mapping method for Electrical Parameters to Model Parameters in IC Aging Simulation Flow
publicationTitle: 2023 International Symposium of Electronics Design Automation (ISEDA)
abstract: With the emerging of semiconductor technology, the typical analytical method does not have the ability to accurately map parameters in the typical aging simulation process, like OMI/TMI, because many non-ideal effects occurred. In this paper, we proposed two multi-task machine learning architectures to map parameters with promising accuracy and speed. One of the architectures is the parallel network, which can handle the interactions between multiple tasks. In order to further digger task correlation and improve accuracy, the cascade network utilizes ensemble learning is proposed. Evaluated on the data generated by the aging simulator, both of the architectures can achieve errors of less than 0.5%.

articleTitle: Transient Noise Simulation Method for Memristor Circuits with Applications
publicationTitle: 2023 International Symposium of Electronics Design Automation (ISEDA)
abstract: Memristor noise simulation is addressed in this paper. Memristor has different noise generation mechanism from the CMOS devices, hence its simulation must be handled in SPICE-type simulators to support memristor-CMOS circuit design. We use the open source NGSPICE as the implementation code base and implement memristor noise simulation based on the existing noise simulation infrastructure. We verify that transient noise simulation can be conducted for circuits including both memristor and CMOS devices. By this enhanced simulation tool we are able to study experimentally the effect of memristor noise on the signal processing accuracy in memristive CMOS analog circuits such as a programmable linear equation solver.

articleTitle: Electronic Quantum Transport Modeling of Monolayer MoS2 Diodes Based on Machine Learning
publicationTitle: 2023 International Symposium of Electronics Design Automation (ISEDA)
abstract: Quantum transport simulation based on first principles has been widely applied to study the transport properties of nanoscale devices. However, such a method is computationally expensive to study large-scale systems, which becomes a key bottleneck in device simulations. To this end, we develop a deep neural network approach to accelerate quantum transport simulations., enabling faster transport calculations while maintaining accuracy for large-scale devices. We studied monolayer Mos2 diodes with different scales as the study system., mapped their atomic structure characteristics to local descriptors as the input of the neural network., and used the non-equilibrium Green's function-density functional theory (NEGF-DFT) method to calculate the electron transmission coefficient of the system as the output of prediction. Our experimental results show that for large-scale devices, quantum transport modeling based on machine learning can achieve acceptable computational efficiency, and our scheme provides a promising solution for breaking the accuracy-efficiency dilemma to achieve large-scale nanodevice simulation.

articleTitle: A Simulation of Noble Gas in Reaction Chamber Based on Direct Simulation Monte Carlo
publicationTitle: 2023 International Symposium of Electronics Design Automation (ISEDA)
abstract: A self-developed Direct Simulation Monte Carlo (DSMC) simulation has been used to model the noble gas in plasma reaction chamber. A Delaunay triangle mesh generator based on Point Insertion Method is completed to improve the adaptability and DSMC code is coupled with unstructured mesh by a new position sample method in triangle and an efficient particle orientation and location technique. After several verification cases, a typical showerhead Chemical Vapor Deposition is modeled and results are shown to illustrate the characteristics of expansion region.

articleTitle: Efficient Improvements of Domain Decomposition Method for Power Grid Transient Simulation
publicationTitle: 2023 International Symposium of Electronics Design Automation (ISEDA)
abstract: The efficiency of large-scale power grid transient simulation has been of great interest. Combined with distributed computing, the domain decomposition method can well tackle this problem. However, the large and dense Schur complement matrix constrains the scalability. Although previous studies reduce the size of the Schur complement matrix by using iterative methods, they become insufficiently stable when encountering asymmetric positive definite problems. In this paper, we propose three techniques to improve the domain decomposition method, including order reduction, pruning, and adaptive number of processes. Order reduction and pruning reduce the computation. Adaptive number of processes increases resource utilization. Combined with the LU factorization, our work can well solve the ill-conditioned problem. Experiments on IBM benchmarks with millions of nodes show that the proposed techniques are all effective. Compared with the traditional domain decomposition method, the performance is improved by 44.16% - 55.34%, and the consumed memory is reduced by 16.66% - 51.35%.

articleTitle: Multi-Scenario Analog and Mixed-Signal Circuit Routing with Agile Human Interaction (Extended Abstract)
publicationTitle: 2023 International Symposium of Electronics Design Automation (ISEDA)
abstract: The expanding markets of emerging applications create large demands for analog and mixed-signal (AMS) integrated circuits. This increasing demand calls for a shorter design cycle and time-to-market period. Routing is one of the most time-consuming and tedious steps in the design cycle. The generation of high-quality routing for AMS circuits still heavily relies on human efforts. Most previous studies only focus on the scenario of pure analog circuit blocks and cannot cover the versatile scenarios from real-world designs with both analog and digital circuit blocks. In this work, we propose an AMS routing engine for designs containing both analog and digital circuit blocks. Through the full cooperation of a multi-scenario routing engine and agile human interaction, the framework can generate high-quality routing solutions for AMS circuits.

articleTitle: Optimization of Redundant Logical Units in RTL Logic Synthesis
publicationTitle: 2023 International Symposium of Electronics Design Automation (ISEDA)
abstract: This paper presents an optimization method for redundant arithmetic logic units in register transfer level (RTL) logic synthesis. An important existing optimization technique for redundant logic units is to merge the same logic units in the circuit, but this method depends very much on specific conditions. Once there are unmet conditions, it cannot be merged, resulting in some waste of work. Therefore, we propose a new optimization method for another possible problem - mutually exclusive logic blocks in the circuit, which can be combined with the existing merging technology to form a more systematic optimization method. Moreover, we have proved through experiments that this method can indeed optimize the circuit to a great extent.

articleTitle: A Novel Schematic Placement and Routing Algorithm for FPGAs
publicationTitle: 2023 International Symposium of Electronics Design Automation (ISEDA)
abstract: As an essential part of FPGA design tools, schematic diagrams must be convenient, fast, readable, and regular for designers to view and modify the circuits. However, placement and routing algorithms limit the the time and effect of generating the diagrams. The existing tools mainly adopt heuristic algorithms, which have a high time cost, or coarse-grained sorting algorithms with poor solution effects. To address these issues, we propose a novel schematic placement and routing algorithm for FPGAs. Aiming at the instability and high timing cost of traditional algorithms for placement and routing, the proposed algorithm (1) adopts heuristic selection for initial value to solve the instability of traditional coarse-grained sorting, and (2) adds score mechanism for fast sorting, and (3) utilizes the backtracking and error correction mechanism to decrease the accumulated errors. Compared with the traditional heuristic algorithm, its complexity is only O(nlogn). The evaluation on the linux system shows that most cases have appropriate crosspoints and less than 10s running time, which demonstrates that our algorithm acquire the balance of the solution result of coarse-grained sorting and the time cost of the heuristic algorithm.

articleTitle: Simulation of Projection Lithography Based on FDTD Method
publicationTitle: 2023 International Symposium of Electronics Design Automation (ISEDA)
abstract: In this paper, projection lithography of thick photoresist (SU-8) is simulated. The imaging theory of projection lens is studied, the mask and projection lens are modeled by vector model. Firstly, the whole algorithm flow is introduced. Vector imaging is used as the theoretical basis of this paper, and a projection lithography simulation model based on FDTD is established. At the same time, the effect of focal plane location on imaging is considered.

articleTitle: Global Routing Under a Congestion-Aware Reinforcement Learning Model
publicationTitle: 2023 International Symposium of Electronics Design Automation (ISEDA)
abstract: As one of the challenging problems in VLSI physical design, global routing is facing increasing difficulties and more and more algorithms attempt to introduce machine learning-based solutions. While most of these solutions lack high enough routability and routing efficiency. In this paper, we propose a congestion-aware reinforcement learning model for global routing. The global routing problem is solved based on pattern routing and a reinforcement learning technique is introduced for better searching global optimal routing decisions. We convert the network relation into a graph structure and introduce a graph attention network to provide global congestion features. Moreover, a net segment-based feature extraction mode for pattern routing is proposed to enhance the routing efficiency. Experimental results on ISPD18 benchmark show that the proposed algorithm can route different unseen layouts with an average routability over 99.9% and the average number of the failed nets is around 6.

articleTitle: Improved Depth-Aware Circuit Partitioning for Mixed Logic Synthesis
publicationTitle: 2023 International Symposium of Electronics Design Automation (ISEDA)
abstract: Mixed logic synthesis takes advantage of distinct logic representations through circuit partitioning, classification and optimization, and merging. How circuits are partitioned plays a significant role in the quality of results (QoR) of mixed logic synthesis. Currently, existing methods employ either a naive or a structurally aware approach. However, the critical path may be destructed by circuit merging due to the critical path segment being disconnected by partitions. To address this issue, we propose an improved depth aware circuit partitioning method for mixed logic synthesis. To be specific, we treat the critical path as an entity and set the partition size dynamically according to the logic depth of the input circuit. Based on the EPFL benchmark suites, XOR-Majority Graph (XMG) achieves a 19% reduction in logic depth with a 6% logic node increase over standard mixed-synthesis.

articleTitle: A Reconfigurable 2D-Mesh NoC Design with Agile Development Technique of SpinalHDL
publicationTitle: 2023 International Symposium of Electronics Design Automation (ISEDA)
abstract: With the development of various application fields, such as automation control, medical technology, and artificial intelligence, the computation complexity and data amount increase significantly, which requires more powerful computing ability of hardware. To this end, both different domain-specific architectures (e.g. TPU) and some typically spatial architectures (e.g. GPU) have integrated more hardware resources to meet the urgent computation demands, bringing huge technique challenges on design scalability. Compared with centralized communication bus protocols (e.g. AMBA Bus), Network-on-Chip (NoC) technique has been widely used in industrial and academic large-scale architecture designs due to the lower latency, higher scalability, and higher bandwidth. Therefore, this paper focuses on parameterized 2D-meshed NOC designs that can support different network sizes, different packet widths, and several routing algorithms. To improve the coding efficiency and reusability, an emerging hardware design language of SpinalHDL embedded in Scala (one high-level language) has been adopted to develop our proposed NoC design. Finally, We measured the area and power consumption of the NoC in different configurations. For example, for a NoC with a size of 16X16, when the data bit width is 64bit and the address bit width is 20bit, the power consumption is 9mW and the area is 64963.5µm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>.

articleTitle: Modeling and Analysis of T-coils with Improved Quality Factor by Patterned Floating/Ground Shields in Millimeter-Wave Regime
publicationTitle: 2023 International Symposium of Electronics Design Automation (ISEDA)
abstract: T-coil, a special inductor which has symmetric coils with center tap, receives widespread adoption in differential circuits and broadband high-order matching networks. In this paper, to investigate and improve its electrical performance, T-coils with three traditional shields and the proposed reduced ladder shield are analyzed and compared by the double-π equivalent circuit model up to 110 GHz. Two-step model parameters extraction flow is established, i.e., linear regression based low frequency extraction and differential evolution based global refinement extraction from DC to 110GHz. Modeling results reveal that the root mean square error between simulated and modeled electrical performance are all below 10%. The T-coil with proposed reduced ladder shield achieves a 3.4% improvement in quality factor in 110 GHz compared with the T-coil with no metal fill. The layout of the optimal shield design is achieved by minimizing the capacitive coupling to the substrate and reducing the resistive loss.

articleTitle: A Physics-Informed Recurrent Neural Network for RRAM Modeling
publicationTitle: 2023 International Symposium of Electronics Design Automation (ISEDA)
abstract: Extracting behavioural models of RRAM devices has been challenging due to their unique “memory” behaviours, for which well-established modeling frameworks and systematic parameter extraction processes have not been available. In this work, we propose a physics-informed recurrent neural network (PiRNN) methodology to generate behavioural models of RRAM devices from practical measurement/simulation data. The proposed framework can faithfully capture the evolution of internal state and its impacts on the output. A series of modifications informed by the RRAM device physics are proposed to enhance the modeling capabilities. Integration strategy with existing SPICE-type simulators is also developed. Numerical experiments with real RRAM devices data demonstrate the feasibility and advantages of the proposed methodology.

articleTitle: Improving Efficiency of Cell-Aware Fault Modeling By Utilizing Defect-Free Analog Simulation
publicationTitle: 2023 International Symposium of Electronics Design Automation (ISEDA)
abstract: Cell-aware fault models of standard cells are critical for test and diagnosis of cell-internal defects in advanced-node technology. Due to the large number of analog simulation times required during the generation of cell-aware fault models, it takes much time and hardware expense to prepare the full models of a technology library. A systematic method is proposed in this paper to improve the generation efficiency of the cell-aware fault models. Voltage information within standard cells from defect-free analog simulation is extracted and then utilized to filter out unnecessary input patterns for targeted defects, which reduces analog simulation times and improves efficiency. Pattern selection strategies for different kinds of defects are designed and explained separately. 2292 cells from a library are chosen to verify the proposed method. Compared to the non-optimized routine, the average number of faulty simulation patterns for each cell are reduced by 44.9% and the end-to-end generation time is reduced to 46.6%.

articleTitle: A Resource Sharing Approach for Logic Synthesis Based on Monte Carlo Tree Search
publicationTitle: 2023 International Symposium of Electronics Design Automation (ISEDA)
abstract: How to reduce the area during multiple logic synthesis algorithms is a key problem. However, it is very hard because there is very small optimization space left for the logic synthesis. To settle this issue, this paper integrates the resource sharing technique into logic synthesis. Resource sharing is a key area-reduction approach in high-level synthesis (HLS), which is an NP-hard problem. Until now, most existing algorithms for resource sharing is greedy approach, which cannot obtain good result especially for the large circuits with numerous function units (FU). This paper proposes a novel algorithm based on Monte Carlo tree search (MCTS) for resource sharing, and uses it to reduce the resources at the early stage of the logic synthesis. The experimental results show the better area with short and stable runtime (0.5 second for MCTS). Comparing to the traditional greedy approach, the proposed algorithm can reduce the number of MUXs' inputs by about 44% and reduce the area up to 20%.

articleTitle: Design and Optimization of FeFET Based CiM for Neural Network Acceleration
publicationTitle: 2023 International Symposium of Electronics Design Automation (ISEDA)
abstract: In the era of the Internet of Things and artificial intelligence, edge devices require low power consumption, realtime, and low hardware cost to address various information processing tasks and corresponding recognition, classification, and learning algorithm models. The compute-in-memory (CiM) architecture reduces the energy consumption and performance loss caused by data movement by integrating computing units into storage and has the potential to solve the “memory wall” problem caused by the Von Neumann architecture, making it a promising direction. The emerging Ferroelectric Field Effect Transistor (FeFET), with its low write power consumption, high CMOS compatibility, and high switching current ratio, has become one of the leading non-volatile memories (NVMs), attracting many researchers to study its application in the CiM architecture. This paper presents a FeFET-based crossbar array design based on the improved 1FeFET-1Resistor(1F1R) memory cell for neural network acceleration.
